dedupe_keys.name: cosmicdancepro tool for orbital decay and network connectivity of leo satellites during solar storms

description: CosmicDancePro is a tool that traces how solar storms raise atmospheric density, change the orbits of low Earth orbit satellites and degrade the network service that users see. The Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur authors built it from space weather measurements, atmospheric density from data-driven and physics-based models, satellite trajectories and network measurement traces, and used it on the Starlink constellation during two major storms, including the May 2024 superstorm. It finds distinct fleet management by Starlink during the storm and quantifies transient outages, latency spikes above 500 ms, up to 60 percent more uplink loss and a drop of more than 10 Mbps in user data rates. Coverage is the Starlink fleet. Format and access: the paper says the tool is open source, but its code link read as private before acceptance, so the code was not found. Licence: CC BY 4.0 for the paper; code licence unknown; free. Caveats: results are for one operator and two storms, and the release status is unconfirmed. It supports hazard exposure and resilience studies of space weather effects on satellite networks. Related catalogue records are the loss of 38 Starlink satellites in February 2022 and the CARL-W Starlink dataset.
